q: 1. According to equation of continuity
explain: For an incompressible fluid, the volume flow rate (Area * Velocity) must remain constant across different sections.

q: 2. A flow through a long pipe at constant rate is called
explain: Constant rate makes it steady; a long pipe of constant diameter makes it uniform.

q: 3. A flow whose streamline is represented by a straight line, is called _________ dimensional flow.
explain: In 1D flow, fluid parameters vary along a single direction, resulting in straight parallel streamlines.

q: 4. The total energy of a liquid particle in motion is equal to
options: pressure energy + kinetic energy + potential energy
explain: Based on Bernoulli's principle, total energy is the summation of these three forms of energy.

q: 5. Which of the following is an example of laminar flow?
options: Flow of oil in measuring instruments
explain: All these cases involve low velocities or high viscosities where the Reynolds number remains very low.

q: 6. The velocity at which the laminar flow stops, is known as ............
explain: The lower critical velocity is the speed below which any flow will eventually become laminar.

q: 7. Reynold's number is the ratio of the inertia force to the ............
explain: $Re = 	ext{Inertia Force} / 	ext{Viscous Force} = ho v D / \mu$.

q: 8. The velocity corresponding to Reynold number of 2800, is called ............
explain: The upper or higher critical velocity corresponds to the Reynolds number where the flow becomes fully turbulent.

q: 9. The loss of pressure head in case of laminar flow is proportional to ...............
explain: According to the Hagen-Poiseuille equation for laminar flow, the pressure drop is directly proportional to the average velocity (v), unlike turbulent flow where it is proportional to v².

q: 10. In a footstep bearing, if the speed of the shaft is doubled, then the torque required to over-come the viscous resistance will be ...............
explain: In viscous lubrication, torque is proportional to the angular velocity (ω). If the speed doubles, the torque also doubles.

q: 11. In a footstep bearing, if the radius of the shaft is doubled, then the torque required to over-come the viscous resistance will be ...............
explain: Torque in a footstep bearing is proportional to the fourth power of the radius (R⁴). Thus, doubling the radius increases torque by 2⁴ = 16 times.

q: 12. A flow is called sub-sonic, if the Mach number is ...............
explain: Sub-sonic flow is defined by a Mach number (M) less than 1 (unity).

q: 13. The ratio of the inertia force to the ............... is called Euler's number.
explain: Euler's number (Eu) is a dimensionless number representing the ratio between pressure forces and inertial forces.

q: 14. Froude's number is the ratio of inertia force to ...............
explain: Froude number (Fr) is a dimensionless number representing the ratio of inertial forces to gravitational forces. It is critical in open channel flow analysis.

q: 15. Reynold's number is the ratio of inertia force to ...............
explain: Reynolds number (Re) quantifies the relative importance of these two types of forces for given flow conditions, guiding whether a flow is laminar or turbulent.

q: 16. A steady uniform flow is through ...............
options: a long pipe at decreasing rate
a long pipe at constant rate
an expanding tube at constant rate
an expanding tube at increasing rate
explain: Uniform flow requires a constant cross-section (long pipe), and steady flow requires a constant discharge (constant rate).

q: 17. The continuity equation ...............
options: expresses the relationship between work and energy
relates the momentum per unit volume between two points on a stream line
relates mass rate of flow along a stream line
requires that Newton's second law of motion be satisfied at every point in fluid
explain: The continuity equation is a mathematical expression of the law of conservation of mass for a fluid system.

q: 18. For solving the problems is hydraulic engineering velocity used is ...............
options: velocity at the centre of pipe section
average velocity of flow over a section
mean of the velocities at the centre and that along the pipe surface
explain: Engineers use average (mean) velocity (V = Q/A) for practical calculations involving discharge and energy equations.

q: 19. For an irrotational flow, the equation (δ²φ/δx²) + (δ²φ/δy²) = 0 given by ...............
explain: This is the Laplace equation. If a velocity potential (φ) satisfies this equation, the flow is irrotational and incompressible.

q: 20. In two dimensional flow the components of velocity are given by u = ax, v = by. The stream lines will be ...............
explain: By integrating dy/dx = v/u = (by)/(ax), we get a power relationship that represents a hyperbolic shape for the streamlines.

q: 21. Bernoulli's equation assumes that ...............
explain: Bernoulli's principle relies on the assumptions of steady, irrotational, incompressible, and non-viscous (frictionless) flow.

q: 22. In a centriyugal pump casing, the flow of water leaving the impeller, is ...............
explain: Once the water leaves the impeller and enters the volute casing, it follows a free vortex path to convert kinetic energy into pressure energy.

q: 23. A pitot tube is used to measure ...............
explain: A pitot tube converts kinetic energy into potential energy at the stagnation point to determine the local velocity of the fluid.

q: 24. The following is not a laminar flow ...............
options: flow in beds in ground water
rise of water in plants through roots
flow of blood in the arteries of human body
explain: Flow in typical water supply pipe lines is usually turbulent due to high velocities and large diameters.

q: 25. To avoid vapourisation, pipe lines are laid over the ridge so that these are above the hydraulic gradient line not more than ...............
explain: To prevent cavitation and the release of dissolved air (which causes air locks), the summit of a pipeline (siphon) should not be more than 6.4 meters above the hydraulic gradient line.

q: 26. The necessary condition for the flow to be uniform is that
options: the velocity is constant at a point with respect to time
the velocity is constant in the flow field with respect to space
the velocity changes at a point with respect to time
explain: Uniform flow occurs when the velocity of flow does not change with respect to space (distance) at any given time (dv/ds = 0).

q: 27. A stream line is a line
options: which is along the path of a particle
which is always parallel to the main direction of flow
across which there is no flow
explain: By definition, the velocity vector is tangent to the streamline at every point; therefore, there is no component of velocity perpendicular to the streamline, meaning no flow crosses it.

q: 28. Bernoulli's theorem deals with the law of conservation of
explain: Bernoulli's theorem states that for an incompressible, non-viscous fluid in steady flow, the sum of pressure energy, kinetic energy, and potential energy per unit mass remains constant, following the law of conservation of energy.

q: 29. Continuity equation deals with the law of conservation of
explain: The continuity equation (A1V1 = A2V2) is based on the principle that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a flow system, representing the conservation of mass.

q: 30. Irrotational flow means
options: the fluid does not rotate while moving
the fluid moves in straight lines
the net rotation of fluid-particles about their mass centres is zero
explain: Irrotational flow is a flow in which the fluid particles do not rotate about their own axes, meaning the curl of the velocity vector is zero.

q: 31. Vorticity is given by
explain: Vorticity is defined mathematically as the curl of the velocity vector, which is exactly equal to twice the angular velocity (rotation).

q: 32. The term p/ρg is known as
explain: The term p/ρg represents the 'Pressure Head', which is the pressure energy of the fluid per unit weight of the fluid.

q: 33. The term Z is known as
explain: In Bernoulli's equation, Z represents the 'Datum Head' or 'Elevation Head', which is the potential energy per unit weight of the fluid.

q: 34. A flow is said to be laminar when
options: the fluid particles move in a zig-zag way
the fluid particles move in layers parallel to the boundary
explain: Laminar flow occurs when fluid particles move in smooth, well-defined paths or layers that do not cross each other.

q: 35. For the laminar flow through a pipe, the shear stress over the cross-section
options: varies inversely as the distance from the centre
varies directly as the distance from the surface
varies directly as the distance from the centre
explain: In a circular pipe, the shear stress distribution is linear, starting from zero at the center and reaching a maximum at the pipe wall. It is directly proportional to the radial distance (r) from the center.

q: 36. For the laminar flow between two parallel plate
explain: For laminar flow between two stationary parallel plates, the velocity distribution is parabolic, and the maximum velocity (at the midpoint) is 1.5 times the average velocity.

q: 37. Hydraulic gradient line (H.G.L.) represents the sum of
options: pressure head, kinetic head and datum head
explain: The Hydraulic Gradient Line (HGL) connects points representing the Piezometric Head, which is the sum of the Pressure Head (p/w) and the Datum Head (z).

q: 38. Mach number is defined as the ratio of
options: viscous force to surface tension force
explain: Mach number is a dimensionless parameter representing the ratio of the inertia force to the elastic force (or the ratio of the velocity of the fluid to the velocity of sound in that fluid).

q: 39. Dynamic similarity between model and prototype means
explain: Dynamic similarity is the similarity of forces; it exists when the ratios of corresponding forces (inertia, viscous, gravity, etc.) at corresponding points are the same.

q: 40. If the depth of flow along the length of the channel is constant, then flow is known as
explain: Uniform flow in an open channel occurs when the depth, discharge, and velocity remain constant at every section along the channel's length.

q: 41. The total energy of flowing water in a channel with respect to bed of channel is known as
explain: Specific energy is the energy per unit weight of water at any section of a channel measured with respect to the channel bed as the datum.
